paragraphs: On Thursday, Mia ran into the school library with big eyes. "There is a nest in the net on the basketball court!" she said. "A small bird flew out of it, and I saw one egg." "Please do not touch the nest," said Teacher Kim. Leo looked up from his poster. "Where is the court? I have never been there," he said. "Go out of the library and walk straight past the hall," said Mia. "Turn left at the big tree, and you will see the court next to the field."

The club walked there together, and Teacher Kim came, too. Tom and Ben stood next to the court with a ball. "We want to practice for the match next week," said Tom. "But we came early today, at seven o'clock, and we saw a bird in the net." "So we did not play," said Ben.

Everybody stood quietly near the net. Nobody spoke. The nest was made of dry grass and leaves. It held a single white egg. Then the bird came back and sat on the nest. It did not move. It was small and brown, and it had a striped head. "It is so beautiful," whispered May. Mia took a photo from far away, so the bird stayed on the nest.

"What kind of bird is it?" asked Lily. Mia opened her fact book and read for a minute. "Many of these birds live in the rainforest," she said, "but some live near people." "The rainforest is far from here," said Leo. "Yes, but this bird chose our school," said Mia. Lily was amazed. She looked at the nest again. "A court is a noisy place," she said, "but this bird has its own quiet home."

"What shall we do?" asked Teacher Kim. Leo had an idea, and he wrote a notice on a big paper. It said, "Please play on the other court. A bird family lives here." Ben held the paper, and Tom put it on the post. Then Tom and Ben carried their ball to the small court near the gate. "Now the bird has a quiet home," said Ben. Mia took one last photo and smiled. "I hope that we will see a baby bird soon," she said.
